name: workspace-memory-bootstrap
purpose: Defines durable memory anchors that an AI agent should load or know how to retrieve before working in this repository.

reader_guide.summary: This is the boot memory contract. A future AI session should be able to open this file and see what must be loaded first, why it matters, and which references shaped the rule.
how_to_read: Read purpose and structure_rules to understand the contract.
Read reference_links to see the internal policies and external memory references behind the design.
Read startup_sequence to know the exact startup loading order.
Read anchors to understand which files are hot, warm, or cold memory.
Run default_command after changing durable rules, navigation, source configs, project boundaries, prompts, workflows, or maps.

structure_rules.rule: Do not rely on chat memory; use this manifest and its anchors as the startup source of truth.
structure_rules.reason: Future sessions may not retain prior conversation context.

structure_rules.rule: Hot anchors must stay within hot_context_limit and contain only context needed before almost every task.
structure_rules.reason: Large startup context wastes tokens and increases stale-context risk.

structure_rules.rule: If a file is mandatory for every future session, add its anchor id to startup_sequence and required_anchor_ids.
structure_rules.reason: A mandatory setting should fail the bootstrap check when it disappears.

structure_rules.rule: Important reference links and internal policy paths must be recorded in reference_links inside this file.
structure_rules.reason: The user should understand the design by opening the setting file alone.

structure_rules.rule: The work summary layer must remain a warm memory anchor and close-out target so future sessions can quickly explain completed work.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly needs to understand later what Codex did by reading repository documents.

structure_rules.rule: The context archive policy must remain a warm memory anchor so future sessions can resume from repository documents when chat context is long or compacted.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked the agent to summarize and archive context proactively when context becomes full.

structure_rules.rule: The user request summary layer must remain a warm memory anchor and close-out target so future sessions can inspect what the user asked for without relying on raw chat.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly requested summaries of their varied prompts and requests to be saved as files.

structure_rules.rule: The request-to-outcome trace layer must remain a warm memory anchor and close-out target so future sessions can inspect what was requested, what happened, and where the result lives.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly requested continuing document management of what requests existed, what work happened, and what each request meant.

structure_rules.rule: The requirements layer must remain a warm memory anchor and close-out target so future sessions can define, review, and build from current requirements instead of only chat instructions.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly wants work to define requirements, keep modifying/reviewing them, and build from them.

structure_rules.rule: The spec-driven layer must remain a warm memory anchor and close-out target so future sessions implement from specs, plans, tasks, validation, and traceability instead of raw prompts.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly requested a structure similar to spec-driven development.

structure_rules.rule: The spec/source reconciliation workflow and template must remain warm memory anchors so future sessions can classify ambiguous spec/source drift before changing either side, and can surface ask_user decisions as clarification_needed alerts.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked for a way to decide whether the spec or source should change and to ask answerable questions through alerts when more detail is needed.

structure_rules.rule: The skill lifecycle layer must remain a warm memory anchor and close-out target so future sessions create, validate, forward-test, and improve skills explicitly.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly noted skill creation was not explicit enough and asked that created skills keep being verified and improved.

structure_rules.rule: Source-code work must record architecture reference sources, at least two architecture options, and architecture decision notes before implementation.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly requires best architecture research before source-code work, not only generic code references.

structure_rules.rule: Source-code work must record the technology stack, stack-specific official docs or standards, version constraints, issue/discussion sources, and community signal interpretation before implementation.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly called out Java/Spring Boot, C, React, Next.js, high-vote Stack Overflow, Reddit, and discussion evidence as technology-specific coding research inputs.

structure_rules.rule: Source-code work must compare maintainable language/runtime options, separate architecture theory from practitioner opinions, and record folder-structure options plus folder semantics before implementation.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked for easy language selection, architecture decisions that consider theory and practitioner disagreement, and folder structures understandable by inspection.

structure_rules.rule: The enterprise/high-quality source registry must remain a warm memory anchor so future sessions can find large-company engineering, research-lab, architecture-center, and high-signal sites without repeating discovery.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked for those site lists to be managed separately.

structure_rules.rule: The broad source discovery registry must remain a warm memory anchor so future sessions can search like a human across global, Korean, Indian, paper, and Korean local review source origins.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked for better web searching with many high-quality sources, Korean big-tech blogs, Indian sources, famous paper discovery, and Korean user review channels.

structure_rules.rule: The marketing evidence profile must remain a warm memory anchor so future sessions can find books, theory, surveys, public statistics, market reports, and quantitative evidence with full numeric provenance.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked for better methods to find marketer research materials, theoretical books, survey evidence, and quantitative numeric support.

structure_rules.rule: Marketing and market-sizing numbers must preserve unit, denominator/base, geography, timeframe, target population, method, sample, sponsor, access date, and comparability notes before use as evidence.
structure_rules.reason: Quantitative claims without context can mislead marketing plans and market sizing.

structure_rules.rule: The web search record layer must remain a warm memory anchor and close-out target so future sessions can inspect prompt-level searches and public decision summaries.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly requires every prompt to start with web search and to leave a text record of the search process without storing raw internal reasoning.

structure_rules.rule: The work mode registry must remain a hot memory anchor so future sessions can select the lightest sufficient operating loop before planning local work.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked to avoid running every loop every time and to support work-type-specific flows plus deferred improvements.

structure_rules.rule: When speed matters or work can split into independent lanes, use parallel-work-planner-agent before parallel execution. Do not run overlapping touch paths or shared mutable resources in the same batch without a dependency, lock, branch/worktree rule, or explicit handoff. When multiple research lanes run in parallel, require a merge gate that waits for all research lanes and releases downstream implementation only after acceptance checks pass.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked for a structure that can process work in parallel when speed is a bottleneck while keeping work understandable and safe.

structure_rules.rule: The installation registry must remain a warm memory anchor because installs change durable dependency or environment state.
structure_rules.reason: Installation records are more critical than ordinary summaries because missing dependency history can break reproducibility and rollback.

structure_rules.rule: The notification settings file must remain a warm memory anchor because future sessions may need to send, dry-run, or disable Slack, Discord, and Teams notifications without exposing secrets.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked for platform notifications controlled through settings while user-provided tokens stay out of the repository.

structure_rules.rule: The root structure policy must remain a warm memory anchor because future sessions need a deterministic way to classify root folders, runtime adapters, local-only scratch, generated outputs, and registered projects.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked to improve any folder-structure contradictions or management friction as the workspace grows.

structure_rules.rule: The assistant runtime adapter registry and tool-agnostic operating model must remain warm memory anchors so future sessions can use the workspace from Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, or another preferred AI coding assistant without policy drift.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly asked for the current Codex-based setup to become a principle template usable from other tools.

refresh_rules: Run this manifest check after changing durable rules, operations navigation, source configs, prompt/workflow maps, or project boundaries.
Keep hot anchors compact; move detailed context to warm or cold anchors.
Update required anchors when a new setting becomes mandatory for every future session.
If a hot anchor becomes stale or too large, split it and record the new path here.
